ALHAMBRA DESIGN REVIEW BOARD

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE

Consistent with Assembly Bill AB 361, the Alhambra Design Review Board meeting will not be physically open
to the public and the meeting will take place via teleconference and video conference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and public
access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Meeting as follows:

Zoom Meeting direct link:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89258373320?pwd=MWQwS0tjZmIvQitjWTJGWTBFRC9Kdz09
Meeting ID: 892 5837 3320 and Password: 403503

Or by telephone by dialing 1 253 215 8782, 1 346 248 7799, 1 669 900 6833, 1 312 626 6799, 1 929 205 6099
or 1 301 715 8592 and entering Meeting ID: 892 5837 3320 and Password: 403503. Please Note: All members
of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed.

For those wishing to speak on an agenda or non-agendized item, you have three options for participation:

  1. Pre-register to speak: Please email Erin Joson at eung@cityofalhambra.org no later than 5:30 p.m. prior
  to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will use when
  calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call or log into the
  meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is
  your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless that time is adjusted by the Chairperson.

  2. “Raise your hand”: For those members of the public that wish to speak, but did not make a request via
  email as described above, such members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand” function
  during the public comments portion, if on Zoom. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is
  your time to speak. If participating via telephone, the Chairperson will ask anyone participating by
  telephone if they would like to speak after asking those on Zoom. Staff will unmute telephone callers
  and you may state you wish to speak.

  3. Email comments to be read into the record, in lieu of speaking: As an alternative to speaking during
  the meeting, you can email your comments by sending them to the Design Review Board by email at
  eung@cityofalhambra.org no later than 5:30 p.m. to ensure that Design Review Board Staff have time
  to print the emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record,
  with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the Chairperson’s
  discretion. If a comment is received after 5:30 p.m. but before the conclusion of the meeting based
  upon its time stamp, or if the sender of the email decides to speak during the meeting, the comment
  will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but will not be read into the record.
  1
 Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should email
or call the Community Development Department at plam@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5034. All requests
for accommodations or translation services shall be made by 4:00 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Design Review
Board meeting. If accommodation or translation is not requested by 4:00 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Design
Review Board meeting, staff will try to accommodate the request to the best of their efforts to provide as much
accessibility as possible while also maintaining public safety. Given the challenges of teleconference and video
conference meetings, all participants are encouraged to email their comments prior to the beginning of the
meeting, but are not required to do so.

PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
Citizens wishing to address the Alhambra Design Review Board on any matter within the
subject matter jurisdiction of the Alhambra Design Review Board not on the Agenda may
do so at this time. Please STATE YOUR NAME AND ADDRESS CLEARLY for the record.

Please note that while the Alhambra Design Review Board values your comments, pursuant
to January 1, 1987 amendments of the Brown Act, the Commission cannot respond nor take
any action until such time as the matter may appear as an item on a forthcoming agenda.

ADJOURNMENT:
The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Alhambra Design Review Board will be held
on Tuesday, February 8, 2022 at 7:30 p.m. Consistent with Assembly Bill AB 361, the
Alhambra Design Review Board meeting will not be physically open to the public and the
meeting will take place via teleconference and video conference.

NOTICE:
AGENDA ITEMS: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each
item of business described hereinabove are on file in the offices of the Community
Development Department in City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California, and are
available for public inspection during regular office hours, which are 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
Monday through Thursday. Should any person have a question concerning any of the above
agenda items prior to the meeting described herein, he or she may contact the Community
Development Director either in person at the Department offices, or by telephone at (626)
570-5034 during regular office hours.

AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT: If you require special assistance to participate in any
City meeting (including assisted listening devices) please contact the Community
Development Department at (626) 570-5034. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the
meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this
meeting.

TRANSLATION SERVICES REQUESTS: If you require translation services in order to
participate in a meeting please contact the Community Development Department at
plam@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5034. All requests for translation services shall be
made by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Design Review Board meeting. If translation is not
requested by 4 p.m. the Thursday prior to the Design Review Board meeting, staff will try to
accommodate the request if possible.

  2
 APPEALS: Any person wishing to appeal any decision of the Design Review Board to the
Planning Commission may do so by filing an appeal in writing along with the appropriate
appeal fee to the Community Development Department in City Hall within 10 calendar days
of the Planning Commission decision. The appeal period for items on this agenda expires at
the close of business on Monday, February 7, 2022.

PROJECT TYPE: This application is for new signage for an existing commercial building.

DESIGN ASSESSMENT: This application proposes new wall signage for an existing
commercial building. The building and adjacent parking lot are located at the corner of
East Valley Boulevard and South Stoneman Avenue. The sign design consists of a company
logo and name in one line with a proposed sign type of internally illuminated channel
letters. The proposal is for a white face with a white trim cap and return, the size and

      Item  2

  ALHAMBRA DESIGN REVIEW BOARD
  REGULAR MEETING
  STAFF REPORT
  111 South First Street
  January 25, 2022
  7:30 P.M.

ADDRESS: 1000 South 5th Street
APPLICANT: Adrian Dahl, Dahl Architects
PROPERTY OWNER: Ko Ko Win
PROJECT TYPE: This application is for a new two-story single-family residence.
PROJECT STATUS: First Time Applicant

DESIGN ASSESSMENT: This application proposes a new single-family residence on a
corner lot at the NE corner of 5th Street and San Marino Avenue. The use is acceptable
with the surrounding homes comprised primarily of one-story residences in a mix of
architectural styles. The neighboring homes are generally authentic in character with a
few exceptions that are pedestrian examples of older remodels. Likewise there are a few
2-story structures in the immediate area along San Marino Avenue. The existing home is
a one-story, post war, ranch-style tract home with a rear yard enclosed by a white painted
CMU site wall.

The proposal is to remove the existing home and replace it with a new 2-story structure.
The massing of the house is defined by 10’ plate heights on the first and second floors.
The volume is further emphasized by a mansard roof. Note that within the last 30 years,
mansard roofs (i.e. a truncated hip roof with a flat roof in the center) have been approved
primarily in commercial fast food structures that utilized that parapet around the flat roof
to hide mechanical equipment. In this residential context the main mansard allows the
building to remain under the 25’ height limit despite the 10’ floors. The resultant massing
does not allow for significant modulation within the building volume to reasonably
complement the scale of the surrounding homes. The volumetric offset on the second
floor is a uniform 5’ which is seen on the two street elevations. The street elevations also
make use of extruded bay window shapes, however, the repetitive shapes appear
additive to the mass which do not help to mitigate the building mass. When you consider
 the scale of the building adjacent to the sidewalk on San Marino Avenue, the two-story
bay window element on the south elevation is actually counterproductive to the setback
of the second floor.

The proposal does not maintain a singular architectural style as is evidenced by the
following attributes. The mansard roof is not authenticated in a traditional single-family
residence. The use of mission tile implies a Spanish or Mediterranean architecture,
however, extensive use of stone veneer is not. If there is a precedent for stone used
extensively on the exterior of a home, it would be based in an English cottage or a more
commonly used Tuscan style. At the north elevation the use of the two-story bay window
element can be seen in a brownstone or victorian residence depending on the detailing
and materials. The wood entry element on the north elevation is detailed in similar
fashion to a craftsman porch using a truss like vernacular and heavy timber supports. This
type of character is occasionally seen in rustic Spanish homes, but there are no
corresponding details that indicate that this is the intent (i.e. shutters, heavy stucco and
a more traditional roof approach). In the same entry element along San Marino Avenue,
there is an arched shaped door element within a full height wall of stone veneer. Due to
the high plate height, the large negative spaces above the window headers are mitigated
by the use of a stucco trim element below the eave. This helps mask the unusual
proportion of the wall space below the eave and above the windows.

The proposal is for a new house, however there is no landscape information. The drawings
state that the area around the house is existing landscape and therefore does not merit
any additional design or documentation. This being a new house will at minimum be
subject to the new MWELO standards and drought resistant landscape. Since the site will
likely be graded for the new structure, it is a natural opportunity to allow the architecture
and the landscape to be developed and designed together.

RECOMMENDATION: Recommendation is for continuance to allow for design revisions
that would better complement the neighboring homes in both scale and architectural
authenticity.

minutes_text:
CITY OF ALHAMBRA DESIGN REVIEW BOARD
  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting

  January 25, 2022

  •  CALL MEETING TO ORDER: 7:30 P.M. via video conference and teleconference

  •  ROLL CALL:
  Present: Ankit Udani, Michael Daninger, Stanley Tsai
  •  Absent: Jose Luis Espinoza, Nora Hernandez
  Staff Present: Richard Abe AIA, Vist Yang

DISCUSSION AGENDA:

ITEM 1:
APPLICANT: 28 East Valley Boulevard
Recommendation action is for approval with the following conditions: 1. The existing pole sign
located north of the property shall be removed; 2. The color of the building paint shall be specified
and submitted to DRB staff for review; and 3. All revised drawings shall be reviewed and
approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance.

MINUTES
The designer was present and there were no public comments submitted prior to the meeting.

The applicant stated that the owner will not be painting the building. She stated that she is fine
with the other conditions.

Tsai stated that there may be minimal contrast since the building will remain the beige color.

Abe stated that the returns could be black to enable a better contrast. This was accepted by the
applicant.

Udani concurred and called for a motion

MOTION:
 •  Tsai moved to approve the application with the following conditions:
  1. The existing pole sign located north of the property shall be removed;
  2. The color of the sign returns and trim caps shall be black;
  3. All revised drawings shall be reviewed and approved by DRB staff prior to permit
  issuance.
   •  The second was by Daninger.
  •  The motion carried 3-0 with the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Ankit Udani, Michael Daninger, Stanley Tsai
Absent: Jose Luis Espinoza, Nora Hernandez

ITEM 2:
APPLICANT: 1000 South 5th Street
Recommended Action is for continuance to allow for design revisions that would better
complement the neighboring homes in both scale and architectural authenticity.

MINUTES
The applicant was present and there were no public comments.

The owner Ko made introductory remarks.

The architect gave a presentation that included the neighborhood map. They showed 2 examples
of two story homes in the area that were similar or inspired the subject design. They also stated
that there was a home on the street that used a flat roof within a hipped configuration. Renderings
were shown that showed the massing of the proposed design. The flat area of the mansard roof
was noted that it could be the location of a solar panel array within the parapet.

Alternatively, the architects showed a possible revision. The ceiling heights of 10’ and 9’ could be
reduced to 9 and 8 feet respectively. There was also a possible use of comp shingle rather than tile
and a hip roof without a mansard. Solar panels could be placed on the south facing shingle roof.
The renderings illustrated the lower, more compatible design.

Tsai stated that he felt that there were too many elements to the house and the architectural style is
not clear. The drawings are also missing information including the distinction of existing and new
trees and site walls. He stated that he felt that the plate heights were too high at 10’. He also
questioned the colors of the project palette.

Daninger stated that he liked moving to a shingle roof rather than tile and reducing the ceiling
heights to 9 and 8 feet. He also stated that a hip rather than a mansard roof is preferable. He noted
that there was a lack of landscape information on the site plan. He questioned if the windows were
clad windows.

The applicant stated that they are wood windows that are clad so they will look like painted wood
windows. They did not have spec sheets or photos of the proposed windows but Daninger
requested they provide those at the next review.

Udani concurred with the other board members and the staff comments. He stated that the
window spacing on the front elevation should be restudied. He also questioned the glass doors at
the entry. The owner stated that he does not want a glass door for the entry. Udani requested more
information on the door specifications. He stated further that the overall massing seems large for
 the context but the proposed height reduction should be helpful. Better more thorough detailing is
also important.

The applicant stated that he appreciated the comments and would revise the design accordingly.

MOTION:
 •  Tsai moved to continue the application.
 •  The second was by Daninger.
 •  The motion carried 3-0 with the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Ankit Udani, Michael Daninger, Stanley Tsai
Absent: Jose Luis Espinoza, Nora Hernandez

ADJOURNMENT:
MOTION:
 •  Michael Daninger moved to adjourn the meeting at 8:20
 •  Seconded by Stanley Tsai
 •  The motion carried 3-0 by the following roll call vote:

Ayes: Ankit Udani, Michael Daninger, Stanley Tsai
Absent: Nora Hernandez, Jose Luis Espinoza

PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED this 8th day of March, 2022.

  _____________________________
  Ankit Udani, Chairman
